en: The Apadāna of the Elder Ambāṭakadāyaka Ekavihārivagga 7 I am a forest-dweller, one who lives alone, A monk who has abandoned all attachments. In the past, I gave a mango fruit To the Buddha, the One with Vision. Because of that gift of an offering, I have attained this state of peace. For eighty-four thousand aeons I was never born in a lower realm. Having passed through many births, I have reached the end of existence. Through the power of that meritorious deed, I have attained the fruit of Arhatship. I have lived for eighty-four thousand years Without ever experiencing illness. My body is free from disease; I am healthy and full of vigor. By the power of that wholesome deed, I have become one who dwells in bliss. I have seen the Truths face to face; I have crossed over the ocean of saṃsāra. I have attained the supreme goal, The state of peace, free from defilements. Through the gift of a single mango, I have reached the end of suffering. Thus, by the power of that merit, I have attained this noble state. May you also give such gifts, And reach the end of suffering as well.
“Having seen the Buddha, the Self-Existent One, the Unconquered, in the forest,
and having taken an ambāṭaka fruit, [he offered it].”
I gave [it] to the Self-Existent One.
In the thirty-first aeon from now,
that was the fruit I gave back then.
I do not recognize any state of woe;
this is the fruit of giving fruit.
Welcome indeed has come to me!
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder Ambāṭakadāyaka speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Ambāṭakadāyaka is the seventh.
